text: To verify a webhook, compute an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body with your endpoint's signing secret and compare it to the Signature header using a constant-time comparison.
Signature checks fail when a framework parses the JSON body before you verify it. Verify against the exact raw bytes received, not a re-serialized object.
Each endpoint has its own signing secret. Using the secret from a test endpoint against live events makes every signature check fail.
Our pricing page lists three plans. The Team plan includes up to ten seats and priority email support.
Reverse proxies and load balancers can rewrite or re-encode request bodies, which breaks signature verification downstream. Pass the body through unchanged.
Signatures include a timestamp. Requests older than five minutes are rejected to prevent replay, so a server clock that drifts can cause verification to fail.
To verify a webhook, calculate an HMAC-SHA256 over the unparsed request body using the endpoint signing secret, then compare it with the Signature header in constant time.
You can export invoices as CSV from the Billing tab. Exports include line items and tax totals.
Webhook deliveries are retried with exponential backoff for up to three days when your endpoint returns a non-2xx status.
Rotating a signing secret keeps the old secret valid for 24 hours, so during rotation you should accept a signature that matches either secret.
The dashboard supports dark mode. Toggle it from your profile menu.
Webhook events are delivered as JSON with an event type field; subscribe only to the event types your integration handles.
